name: Charlottesville Radionuclide Station
notes: Automated particulate aerosol sampler and SAUNA noble gas xenon detection system monitoring eastern North American airmasses.

name: Ashland Radionuclide Station
notes: Central US continental atmospheric particulate and radioxenon monitoring facility.

name: Oahu Radionuclide Station
notes: Key mid-Pacific particulate and radioxenon monitoring station for trans-Pacific plume detection.

name: Schauinsland Radionuclide Station
notes: Ultra-low-background mountain observatory in the Black Forest; reference noble gas monitoring lab for Central Europe.

name: French Guiana Radionuclide Station
notes: Equatorial aerosol monitoring station covering equatorial Atlantic and South American trade winds.

name: Takasaki Radionuclide Station
notes: Primary East Asian monitoring facility that detected prompt radioxenon releases from DPRK underground nuclear tests in 2006, 2009, and 2013.

name: Dubna Radionuclide Station
notes: Western Russian radioxenon and particulate monitoring station co-located with nuclear physics research center.

name: Ussuriysk Radionuclide Station
notes: Key Far East Russian station situated within atmospheric sampling range of North Korean test sites.

name: Melbourne Radionuclide Station
notes: Southern Ocean and Australasian atmospheric radionuclide surveillance point operated by ARPANSA.

name: Pelindaba Radionuclide Station
notes: Southern African continental surveillance point monitoring South Atlantic and Indian Ocean air masses.

name: Matsushiro Primary Seismic Station
notes: High-sensitivity borehole array in crystalline granite bedrock. Key station for regional teleseismic detection of DPRK test events.

name: Pinedale Primary Seismic Station
notes: North American primary seismic array monitoring global underground explosive source signatures.

name: Warramunga Primary Seismic Array
notes: 24-element cross-shaped aperture seismic array situated on stable Precambrian craton with exceptional signal-to-noise ratio.

name: NORSAR Primary Seismic Array
notes: World-renowned Scandinavian seismic array; historical pioneer in distinguishing natural earthquakes from underground explosions.

name: GERES Primary Seismic Array
notes: 25-element high-frequency regional seismic array in Central Europe.

name: Makanchi Primary Seismic Array
notes: Central Asian seismic array situated adjacent to former Semipalatinsk test grounds and Chinese Lop Nur testing region.

name: Pinon Flat Infrasound Array
notes: 8-element spatial wind-filter microbarometer array detecting atmospheric shockwaves and acoustic gravity waves.

name: Brimont Infrasound Station
notes: Western European infrasound array for atmospheric blast and bolide detection.

name: Aktobe Infrasound Station
notes: Eurasian continental infrasound array monitoring upper-atmospheric shock propagation.

name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Infrasound
notes: North Pacific rim infrasound array monitoring high-latitude atmospheric and volcanic events.

name: Cape Leeuwin Hydroacoustic Station
notes: Tripartite moored hydrophone station deployed in the Southern Ocean deep sound SOFAR channel.

name: Juan Fernandez Hydroacoustic Station
notes: South Pacific SOFAR channel hydroacoustic mooring detecting oceanic underwater detonations across thousands of kilometers.

name: Diego Garcia Hydroacoustic Station
location: Diego Garcia, British Indian Ocean Territory
notes: Dual-node moored hydrophone array monitoring the entire Indian Ocean basin.

name: Ascension Island Hydroacoustic Station
notes: South Atlantic equatorial hydrophone array monitoring sub-surface acoustic propagation.
